top.line: Seven questions a healthcare team asked before real patient data went into sgit vaults, answered.
top.para: And QR codes for passing keys and links.

in-short.line: Good questions; no live date; your region; erasure works; lose the key, lose the vault; tokens; QR codes.

context.line: A team designing patient vaults with invented data asked before using any real data.

live.line: No date: test on dev with invented data, and run your own server at the version you tested.
live.para: Then the live date is yours.

address.line: The patient's details live in their own vault, opened from a link the clinic gives them.
address.para: Ideally sealed to their key, as a QR code.

region.line: Whichever region you choose, in your own AWS account; the host holds ciphertext only.

erasure.line: A deleted vault is removed and its id can never be uploaded again; without a key, copies are unreadable.
erasure.para: Deletion stops future access, not past copies.

backup.line: Lose the clinic key, lose the vaults: seal it to custodians, keep an offline QR copy, rotate on departures.

tokens.line: The server token only authorises uploads; changes need the vault key and identity.

append.line: Append lanes: write-only, per sender, sealed to the clinic's key, from any page.

qr.line: Public keys swapped by QR code, vault links sealed to a patient's key, the clinic key backed up sealed.

limits.line: No live date; not legal advice; lane routes on dev when documented; deletion is not retroactive.

sources.line: The team's questions, my answers, sgit.ai docs, the deploy guides and pki.sgit.ai.
